title: React DOM rendering modes hydration and host integration
concepts: A renderer maps React's platform-independent element and component model onto a host environment such as the browser DOM.
Client rendering creates and updates the host tree in a browser. Server rendering produces HTML before client JavaScript runs; hydration attaches React behavior to compatible server-produced markup.
Streaming can send completed portions of server-rendered HTML before the full response is ready. Suspense boundaries can define units of fallback and progressive delivery.

Hydration requires the initial client output to match the server HTML. Mismatches signal inconsistent data, environment-dependent rendering, or invalid markup and should be corrected rather than hidden.
Selective hydration prioritizes boundaries the user interacts with, while progressive enhancement ensures meaningful server output can exist before all client code loads.

Static prerendering waits for content before producing a static response; streaming rendering can emit available content incrementally. Runtime stream capabilities and framework integration determine which mode is available.
React's rendering APIs and the framework's routing, cache, and request lifecycle are separate layers. Select an API based on host runtime, response mode, interactivity, and framework support.
